{
  "change_type": "major",
  "title": "Inference-Time Perception Monitoring for VLMs via Complementary Process Reward Distillation",
  "core_problem": "Vision-language models (VLMs) performing multi-step visual reasoning suffer from 'evidence collapse' — progressively losing visual grounding during reasoning even as they produce confident text (Don't Blink, arXiv 2604.04207). While lightweight probes on VLM hidden states can detect hallucination risk pre-generation (HALP achieves 0.93 AUROC) and training-time perception RL methods improve perception quality, NO existing approach provides near-zero-cost STEP-LEVEL PROCESS monitoring during generation that DECOMPOSES perception errors from reasoning errors. Pre-generation probes cannot catch errors that emerge mid-reasoning due to evidence collapse; external PRMs (Perceval, URSA, VisualPRM) provide step-level monitoring but require full model forward passes per verification step; and training-time perception RL (MoCA, PEARL, PAPO, VPPO) improves the base model but offers no inference-time detection mechanism. Recent online monitoring approaches partially address this: PSRD (arXiv 2604.17982) achieves 50% hallucination reduction via phase-wise self-reward decoding, but only on descriptive captioning tasks (not multi-step math reasoning), at 4× inference cost, and without any perception/reasoning error decomposition. VerifySteer (arXiv 2605.20745) discovers that verifier strictness is encoded at step boundaries in hidden states, but operates exclusively on text-only LLMs and cannot monitor visual evidence. SIEVE (arXiv 2603.14117) provides visual evidence re-engagement via internal representations, but offers no error monitoring or decomposition — it re-engages vision without knowing WHEN or WHY re-engagement is needed. Can we distill step-level perception-error expertise from multimodal PRMs into a near-zero-cost auxiliary head that monitors evidence collapse in real time, providing DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning error signals that enable TARGETED interventions at each reasoning step?",
  "opportunity": "A precise technical gap exists at the intersection of four established capabilities: (1) VLM hidden states encode reliable visual evidence and correctness signals — probes achieve 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection (HALP), 0.96 AUROC for correctness prediction (Gnosis), and >92% accuracy for reliability flagging (arXiv 2508.18297). SWIFT (KDD 2026, arXiv 2505.12225) shows that even <0.005% parameter linear transformations on hidden states can serve as effective reward models — validating extreme efficiency. LiLaVe (arXiv 2504.16760) demonstrates lightweight latent verifiers reliably extract correctness from LLM hidden states. (2) Multimodal PRMs encode rich STEP-LEVEL perception-error expertise — URSA-RM-8B's DualMath-1.1M dataset with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, VisualPRM-8B's 400K process supervision samples, EVPV's explicit visual premise verification achieving 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench — that captures error PATTERNS across steps, not just binary outcomes. (3) VLMs demonstrably suffer from evidence collapse during multi-step reasoning — 'Don't Blink' shows 53-90% loss of visual attention mass as reasoning unfolds, with the 'confident-but-blind' pattern causing 15-40pp higher error rates. (4) Complementary approaches provide re-engagement mechanisms but not monitoring: SIEVE re-engages visual evidence via internal representations achieving 8% average gain; DLR (arXiv 2604.07518) provides step-wise visual re-grounding via learned latent queries; Entropy-Gradient Grounding (arXiv 2604.08456) offers training-free evidence retrieval. These re-engagement methods need a TRIGGER — they lack the ability to detect WHEN and WHY re-engagement is needed. The gap: existing online monitoring approaches (PSRD) operate on descriptive captioning only, cost 4× inference time, and treat all hallucinations uniformly without decomposition; step-boundary hidden-state signals (VerifySteer) work only for text-only LLMs; evidence re-engagement methods (SIEVE, DLR) lack monitoring capability; and existing probes (HALP, VIB-Probe, EnsemHalDet, SWIFT, LiLaVe) operate on OUTCOME-LEVEL binary labels without step-level process understanding or error-type decomposition. The opportunity: PRM-distilled step-level supervision provides richer training signal than either binary outcome labels (used by HALP/SWIFT/LiLaVe) or self-reward signals (used by PSRD), capturing temporal error patterns (how evidence collapse propagates across steps) and error-type decomposition (perception vs. reasoning) that outcome-supervised probes and self-reward mechanisms inherently cannot learn. This enables a monitoring head that detects evidence collapse AS IT HAPPENS during generation, at probe-level cost but with PRM-level process understanding — and critically, provides DECOMPOSED error signals that can trigger TARGETED interventions (image re-examination for perception errors, backtracking for reasoning errors) rather than one-size-fits-all corrections.",
  "landscape": "**VLM Hidden-State Probing for Error Detection (established but limited to outcome-level):** HALP (EACL 2026, arXiv 2603.05465) trains lightweight 3-layer MLP probes on VLM hidden states, achieving 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection pre-generation across 8 modern VLMs — the most direct baseline for any auxiliary-head approach. Key finding: late query-token states integrating vision+language are most predictive. VIB-Probe (arXiv 2601.05547, Jan 2026) applies variational information bottleneck to VLM attention heads, achieving 95.92% AUROC on POPE with inference-time mitigation capability. EnsemHalDet (arXiv 2604.02784, Apr 2026) trains ensemble of logistic regression classifiers on hidden states + attention, achieving 0.874 AUC at <0.002s per sample. 'Reading Between the Lines' (arXiv 2511.19806) trains 4-layer MLP probes on VLM hidden states specifically for OCR perception errors — finding intermediate layers 15-20 most informative. 'Anatomy of a Lie'/CAD (arXiv 2603.15557, Mar 2026) uses information-theoretic probes mapping VLM generation to a 'Cognitive State Space' and decomposes hallucinations into perceptual instability, inferential conflict, and decisional ambiguity — sharing our decomposition motivation but using unsupervised anomaly detection rather than PRM-distilled supervision. LiLaVe (arXiv 2504.16760, Apr 2025) introduces lightweight latent verifiers that extract correctness signals from LLM hidden states with significantly reduced computational overhead — validating the probe paradigm for verification but operating at outcome level on text-only LLMs. SWIFT (KDD 2026, arXiv 2505.12225) mines intrinsic rewards from LLM hidden states via single linear transformation with <0.005% parameters, achieving 12.7% higher accuracy than EurusRM-7B on MATH — the most parameter-efficient hidden-state reward approach, but text-only and outcome-level. KEY LIMITATION: All these probes train on binary outcome labels (correct/hallucinated) and operate pre-generation or per-response. None provides step-level process monitoring during multi-step reasoning, none can detect evidence collapse as it unfolds across steps, and none decomposes perception from reasoning errors. **Internalized Verification (near-zero-cost but step-agnostic):** Gnosis (arXiv 2512.20578, Dec 2025) trains ~5M parameter self-awareness heads (two-stream: hidden state + attention encoders with gated MLP fusion) achieving 0.96 AUROC, outperforming external judges including Gemini 2.5 Pro — demonstrating that tiny modules can rival massive verifiers. LaSeR (arXiv 2510.14943, Oct 2025) uses last-token self-rewarding via closed-form RL objective, achieving ~80% verification F1 at one-token cost. ReProbe (arXiv 2511.06209) trains <10M param probes matching 7B PRMs. STEP (arXiv 2601.09093) uses hidden states as early signals for trace evaluation. REVERSE (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2504.13169) trains VLMs for on-the-fly self-verification during generation via retrospective resampling, reducing hallucinations by up to 34%. VeriThinker (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2505.17941) trains LLMs to verify then generate. ADPO (arXiv 2601.01483) jointly trains generation + outcome-level verification. KEY LIMITATION: All internalized verifiers either (a) operate at outcome level only (Gnosis, LaSeR, ADPO, LiLaVe, SWIFT), (b) use binary labels without error-type decomposition (all), or (c) operate on text-only hidden states missing visual features (ReProbe, STEP, LaSeR, SWIFT, LiLaVe). None combines PRM-distilled step-level supervision with multimodal hidden states for decomposed perception/reasoning monitoring. **Online Monitoring During Generation (emerging but limited):** PSRD (arXiv 2604.17982, Apr 2026) achieves online hallucination monitoring during VLM generation via phase-wise self-reward decoding — discovering that hallucination severity peaks at phase onsets and using a CLIP-based reward model for guided intervention. Achieves 50% CHAIR reduction on LLaVA-1.5-7B with 4× inference overhead. KEY LIMITATIONS: (a) tested exclusively on descriptive captioning/visual understanding (AMBER, POPE, Object HalBench) — no multi-step mathematical reasoning evaluation; (b) treats all hallucinations uniformly without perception/reasoning decomposition; (c) 4× inference cost is substantially higher than probe-level monitoring; (d) uses self-elicited signals which capture surface-level confidence patterns rather than systematic error expertise. VerifySteer (arXiv 2605.20745, May 2026) discovers that verifier strictness is encoded in hidden states at paragraph-boundary delimiter tokens (layer 22, double-newline tokens), enabling selective latent steering that matches self-consistency at 4-7× less compute. KEY LIMITATIONS: (a) exclusively text-only LLM — no visual modality, cannot monitor visual evidence collapse; (b) addresses verifier calibration (over-critical vs under-critical), not evidence collapse detection; (c) no error-type decomposition (perception vs reasoning). PSRD and VerifySteer together validate two key premises of our approach — that online monitoring during generation is valuable (PSRD) and that hidden states at step boundaries encode useful signals (VerifySteer) — but neither provides MULTIMODAL, DECOMPOSED, NEAR-ZERO-COST step-level monitoring. **Evidence Collapse and Visual Grounding Loss / Re-engagement:** 'Don't Blink' (arXiv 2604.04207, Apr 2026) demonstrates that VLMs lose 53-90% of attention to visual evidence during multi-step reasoning — the 'evidence collapse' phenomenon. Proposes a 'vision veto' policy detecting 'confident-but-blind' predictions via entropy-vision interaction models at zero additional cost. 'Seeing but Not Believing' (arXiv 2510.17771, Oct 2025) shows VLMs encode reliable visual evidence in deep layers but under-utilize it. SPARC (arXiv 2602.06566) separates perception/reasoning circuits for test-time scaling. SIEVE (arXiv 2603.14117, Mar 2026) is an end-to-end self-revisit framework that re-engages visual evidence during reasoning via internal representations — using gradient saliency to identify textual anchors, matching to image patches via cosine similarity in middle-layer hidden states, and injecting cached region embeddings back into the reasoning chain. Trained via RL (GRPO), achieves 8% average improvement across visual reasoning benchmarks. KEY INSIGHT: SIEVE provides a concrete RE-ENGAGEMENT mechanism but not a monitoring mechanism — it learns when to re-engage via RL policy without explicitly diagnosing error types. DLR (arXiv 2604.07518, Apr 2026) decomposes reasoning into premise-look-reason cycles with learned latent visual grounder using 32 learnable queries, achieving MathVista 67.5%. Entropy-Gradient Grounding (arXiv 2604.08456, Apr 2026) provides training-free evidence retrieval via entropy-gradient relevance maps — using next-token distribution entropy backpropagated to visual embeddings for region localization. KEY INSIGHT: evidence collapse is a TEMPORAL phenomenon — models may start well-grounded and become blind by step 3 — making pre-generation probes insufficient and step-level monitoring essential. Re-engagement methods (SIEVE, DLR, Entropy-Gradient Grounding) address the RESPONSE but not the DETECTION; PAMH provides the detection signal that can trigger these interventions. **Training-Time Perception-Aware RL (training-only, no inference monitoring):** MoCA (ICML 2026 Spotlight, arXiv 2605.14054) — modality-aware credit assignment, 73.8 MathVista. PEARL (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2511.18437) — perception checklists, +9.7% MathVerse. PDCR (arXiv 2605.13467) — decomposed confidence rewards. PRCO (arXiv 2603.28618) — Observer/Solver coevolution. PAPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2507.06448) — implicit perception loss, 30.5% perception error reduction. VPPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.09285) — visual dependency advantages. PeBR (arXiv 2509.13031) — two-stage perception-first RL. Perception-R1 (arXiv 2506.07218) — visual perception reward. 'From Seeing to Thinking' (arXiv 2605.20177) — staged perception-then-reasoning. G1 (arXiv 2505.13426) — perception-reasoning mutual bootstrapping. PROPA (arXiv 2511.10279) — MCTS+GRPO process-level optimization. Vision-SR1 (arXiv 2508.19652) — self-rewarding VLM via reasoning decomposition into visual and language components with decoupled reward-advantage framework; shares our perception/reasoning decomposition motivation but operates at training time, not inference monitoring. ViCrit (arXiv 2506.10128) — verifiable RL proxy task training VLMs to localize synthetic visual hallucinations injected into captions; improves perception but provides no inference-time monitoring. None provides inference-time step monitoring. **External Multimodal PRMs (rich supervision sources, expensive at inference):** URSA-RM-8B (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2501.04686) — DualMath-1.1M training data with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, SAM-B+SigLIP-L+Qwen2.5-Math architecture. Model weights released on HuggingFace (URSA-MATH/URSA-RM-8B). VisualPRM-8B (arXiv 2503.10291) — 8B VLM PRM trained on VisualPRM400K with VisualProcessBench (2,866 samples, 26,950 human-annotated step labels). Model weights and benchmark fully released (OpenGVLab). Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, Apr 2026) provides perception-centric PRM with token-level error grounding and truncation-regeneration. NOTE: code and model weights NOT yet released as of May 2026 despite the paper's claim; the RUCAIBox/Perceval GitHub repository does not exist. EVPV/'Grounding the Score' (arXiv 2603.16253) — decouples perceptual from reasoning errors via explicit visual premise verification, SOTA 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench. Code released (github.com/Qwen-Applications/EVPV-PRM). VL-PRM (arXiv 2509.23250) — shows smaller VL-PRMs match larger ones. MM-PRM (arXiv 2505.13427) — 700K+ MCTS-based step annotations. Athena-PRM (arXiv 2506.09532) — SOTA with only 5K samples. VRPRM (arXiv 2508.03556) — first multimodal Chain-of-Thought PRM trained via RL with 3.6K CoT PRM examples + 50K standard PRM data, achieving up to 118% relative improvement over base model. CoRGI (arXiv 2508.00378, withdrawn) — proposed step-wise claim decomposition with post-hoc visual grounding and verification across VCR, ScienceQA, MMMU, MathVista. **VLM Self-Correction:** Octopus-8B (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.08503) achieves SOTA VLM self-correction (82.1% MathVista) via correction-specific rollout augmentation. 'Aha Moment Revisited' (arXiv 2506.17417) shows VLM self-verification consistently underperforms majority voting. Sherlock (arXiv 2505.22651) finds self-correction activates in <10% of samples. **Our unique position:** We are the first to distill STEP-LEVEL PROCESS reward signals (not binary outcomes, not self-reward) from multimodal PRMs into a near-zero-cost auxiliary head that monitors evidence collapse during generation with DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning error signals enabling TARGETED interventions. The closest comparisons: (a) HALP/VIB-Probe/SWIFT/LiLaVe — probe hidden states but use outcome labels, no step-level process monitoring, no error decomposition; (b) PSRD — provides online monitoring but captioning-only, 4× cost, no decomposition, no math reasoning; (c) VerifySteer — discovers step-boundary signals but text-only LLM, no visual modality; (d) Gnosis — near-zero-cost internalized verification but outcome-level only; (e) EVPV — decomposes perception from reasoning errors but operates as external PRM; (f) SIEVE/DLR — provide re-engagement mechanisms but no error monitoring/decomposition; (g) CAD — decomposes error types via probes but uses unsupervised anomaly detection without PRM-distilled supervision; (h) Vision-SR1 — decomposes visual/language reasoning but at training time only.",
  "inspired_by": "Untried combination: 'evidence collapse phenomenon (Don't Blink) + PRM step-level process expertise (URSA-RM/VisualPRM/EVPV) + lightweight probe feasibility (HALP/Gnosis/SWIFT) + training-time perception RL complementarity (MoCA/PEARL) + visual re-engagement mechanisms (SIEVE/DLR) as intervention targets.' The key insight emerges from analyzing limitations of recent online monitoring approaches: PSRD (Apr 2026) proves online monitoring during generation reduces hallucination by 50% but only on captioning at 4× cost without decomposition; VerifySteer (May 2026) proves step-boundary hidden states encode verification signals but only in text-only LLMs. PRM-distilled process supervision provides something neither self-reward (PSRD) nor training-free steering (VerifySteer) can: SYSTEMATIC error patterns encoding how perception errors differ from reasoning errors, how evidence collapse propagates across steps, and what specific visual misinterpretation patterns look like (from URSA's 302K curated misinterpretation corpus and EVPV's explicit premise verification). Furthermore, SIEVE/DLR demonstrate effective visual re-engagement mechanisms (injecting cached region embeddings, premise-conditioned latent grounding) that serve as natural intervention targets when PAMH detects perception errors — creating a monitoring→targeted-intervention pipeline. Innovation pattern: 'Signal enrichment + targeted intervention' — HALP proves the probe architecture works; PSRD proves online monitoring is valuable; we ask what happens when you combine probe-level cost (SWIFT-validated efficiency) with PRM-level process understanding (richer than self-reward), targeting the specific unsolved problem (multimodal evidence collapse during math reasoning) where decomposed error signals enable differentiated interventions.",
  "approach": "Architecture: Perception-Aware Monitoring Head (PAMH). Augment a Qwen3-VL-8B policy with a lightweight auxiliary monitoring module inspired by Gnosis's two-stream design: (1) a hidden-state stream — 2-layer MLP (hidden dim 256, ReLU) reading from intermediate layers 16-24 (informed by 'Reading Between the Lines' finding that intermediate layers are most informative for perception errors, nuancing 'Seeing but Not Believing' which emphasizes deep layers for evidence encoding), and (2) an attention-engagement stream — lightweight 1D convolution extracting visual attention mass trajectory features (inspired by 'Don't Blink's evidence collapse metric). Both streams fuse via gated linear projection to produce step-quality scores. Total parameters: ~3-5M (<0.1% of 8B policy), validated as feasible by SWIFT's demonstration that even <0.005% parameter transformations can serve as effective reward models. The head predicts decomposed step-quality scores: P(perception_error | h_t, a_t) and P(reasoning_error | h_t, a_t) at each step boundary, providing error-type-specific monitoring motivated by MoCA's insight (different error types require different interventions), CAD's decomposition framework (perceptual instability vs. inferential conflict), and Vision-SR1's finding that decomposing visual from language reasoning enables targeted optimization.\n\nTraining Pipeline (4 phases):\n\nPhase 0 — Perception-Aware RL Base (modular, optional). Apply perception-aware RL training to Qwen3-VL-8B following the PEARL paradigm: construct perception checklists for training problems, use dual-branch GRPO with perception rewards (lambda=0.1). This establishes a strong base model with improved perception. We test with and without this phase to quantify complementarity.\n\nPhase 1 — Multi-PRM Trajectory Scoring & Step-Level Signal Extraction (REDESIGNED for availability). Sample ~50K multimodal math reasoning trajectories from the (optionally perception-RL-trained) Qwen3-VL-8B policy across MathV360K, GeoQA, and MMathCoT problems. Score with AVAILABLE teacher PRMs (all confirmed released as of May 2026): (a) URSA-RM-8B (PRIMARY — released on HuggingFace URSA-MATH/URSA-RM-8B, DualMath-1.1M training data with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, SAM-B+SigLIP-L+Qwen2.5-Math architecture, covers the same 6 mathematical benchmarks as our evaluation), (b) VisualPRM-8B (SECONDARY — released on HuggingFace OpenGVLab/VisualPRM-8B, trained on VisualPRM400K, provides step-level process supervision with VisualProcessBench-compatible scoring), (c) EVPV (COMPLEMENTARY — code released at github.com/Qwen-Applications/EVPV-PRM, provides DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning labels via explicit visual premise verification, SOTA 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench). AVAILABILITY CONTINGENCY: Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583) would be an ideal additional teacher given its token-level perception-centric error grounding and Qwen-VL family compatibility, but its code/weights are NOT released as of May 2026 (RUCAIBox/Perceval GitHub does not exist). If Perceval is released during the project, we incorporate it as a fourth teacher; otherwise, URSA-RM-8B + VisualPRM-8B + EVPV provide sufficient coverage: URSA-RM-8B contributes systematic misinterpretation patterns, VisualPRM-8B contributes broad step-level process scores, and EVPV uniquely contributes the perception/reasoning decomposition labels essential for PAMH's dual-head training. Extract THREE types of step-level signals beyond binary labels: (i) PRM score DROP trajectories — how error propagates across steps (temporal process patterns that outcome labels cannot capture), (ii) perception-specific error flags from EVPV's visual premise verification (which steps involve perceptual vs. reasoning errors), cross-validated with URSA-RM-8B's misinterpretation-insertion labels, (iii) evidence collapse indicators — attention mass decrease between consecutive steps (from 'Don't Blink' methodology applied to training trajectories). Validate via human annotation on 500-sample subset measuring inter-PRM agreement and error-type classification accuracy.\n\nPhase 2 — PAMH Training with Process-Level Supervision. Three-stage curriculum: (2a) Warm-up: freeze VLM backbone, train PAMH on PRM-labeled trajectories with multi-task loss: binary cross-entropy for perception-error and reasoning-error heads PLUS auxiliary regression loss predicting step-level PRM score (providing richer gradient than binary labels alone — this is the key difference from HALP-style direct probing and SWIFT-style outcome-level reward extraction). Layer selection: intermediate layers 16-24 as primary features based on 'Reading Between the Lines' findings, with ablation against deep layers 24-32 ('Seeing but Not Believing'). (2b) Joint fine-tuning: unfreeze backbone with gradient scaling (lambda=0.1-0.3) on PAMH loss, KL regularization (beta=0.01) against original policy to preserve perception RL improvements from Phase 0. (2c) Perception-error curriculum: oversample trajectories exhibiting evidence collapse (identified by attention mass decrease >50% between steps 1 and step N) and EVPV-flagged visual misinterpretation, weighted 3x.\n\nPhase 3 — Inference-Time Monitoring with Targeted Intervention Protocol. During generation, PAMH provides step-quality estimates at each step boundary (identified analogously to VerifySteer's paragraph-boundary approach, but operating on multimodal hidden states). Monitoring is decomposed with TARGETED interventions: (a) When P(perception_error) exceeds calibrated threshold tau_p, trigger SIEVE-inspired visual evidence re-engagement — inject cached region embeddings from gradient-salient image patches back into the reasoning chain (leveraging SIEVE's validated mechanism that middle-layer hidden states enable effective cross-modal matching without image re-encoding). This is more compute-efficient than Perceval's truncation-regeneration (which requires full response regeneration) and more targeted than PSRD's contrastive decoding (which adjusts decoding globally without diagnosing the error type). (b) When P(reasoning_error) exceeds tau_r, trigger standard backtracking and re-generation of the current step. Thresholds calibrated on held-out validation set targeting >80% precision (motivated by 'Don't Blink' finding that false alarms in visual tasks waste compute on benign disengagement). COST ANALYSIS: The PAMH forward pass adds <0.1% compute per step (~0.05ms for 3-5M params). <result>Now I have comprehensive details on all six papers. Let me compile the findings.

---

Here are detailed findings on all six papers:

---

## 1. LiLaVe (arXiv 2504.16760) -- Lightweight Latent Verifiers

**Authors:** Bartosz Piotrowski, Witold Drzewakowski, Konrad Staniszewski, Piotr Milos (April 2025)

**How it works:** LiLaVe extracts hidden states from the base LLM at specific layers and token positions, then trains a lightweight classifier to predict answer correctness. It extracts from layers {-1, -2, -4, -8, -16} and the last 16 token positions, yielding 80 hidden-state vectors per generation (5 layers x 16 tokens), each of dimension 4096 (for Llama 3.1 8B).

**Architecture:** After ablation studies comparing logistic regression, MLP, and SwiGLU variants, the authors selected **XGBoost** as the core classifier (max tree depth 5, learning rate 0.1). Training takes approximately 3 minutes on CPUs. This is notably different from neural approaches -- it is a gradient-boosted tree ensemble operating on concatenated hidden-state features.

**Training:** 1,000 examples per benchmark with multiple generations at five temperatures {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}. Binary correctness labels. Standard classification loss.

**Results (AUC for correctness prediction):**
- GSM8K: 0.86 (vs ORM-DeepSeek 0.88, ORM-Mistral 0.81)
- MATH500: 0.88 (vs ORM-DeepSeek 0.90)
- algebra_linear_1d: 0.93 (vs ORM-DeepSeek 0.90)
- GSM-Symbolic-p2: 0.78 (vs ORM-DeepSeek 0.75)

LiLaVe approaches or matches multi-billion-parameter ORM verifiers while being orders of magnitude cheaper. It supports best-of-N, weighted majority voting, conditional self-correction, and conditional majority voting strategies. Tested on Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 2 2B, and Phi-3.5-mini.

---

## 2. ELHSR / "Reward Inside the Model" (arXiv 2505.12225)

**Authors:** Jizhou Guo, Zhaomin Wu, Philip S. Yu (May 2025)

**Architecture (exact details):** For each token, ELHSR concatenates hidden states across ALL L transformer layers: `h_t = [h_t^1; h_t^2; ...; h_t^L] in R^{Ld}`. A single linear transformation produces both a gating value and a reward value:

```
[g_tilde_t, r_t] = W_ELHSR * h_t + b_ELHSR
```

Where `W_ELHSR in R^{2 x Ld}` and `b_ELHSR in R^2`. The gate passes through sigmoid; the final score is `R = sum(g_t * r_t) / max(sum(g_t), epsilon)` -- a gated weighted average of per-token rewards.

**Parameter count:** O(L x d) parameters. For Llama-3.1-8B (32 layers, 4096 hidden dim): approximately **270K parameters**, which is **<0.005%** of EurusRM-7B's 7.1B parameters. This is the paper's headline efficiency claim.

**Training:** Binary cross-entropy loss. 6,000 instances per dataset (8 reasoning paths each = 48K samples). Early stopping.

**Results (Best-of-N accuracy):**
- MATH average across 3 LLMs: **57.5** (vs best baseline 52.9)
- GSM8K average: **89.0** (vs best baseline 88.2)
- AQuA_RAT average: **72.8** (vs best baseline 70.2)

Outperforms EurusRM-7B, Skywork-Reward-8B, Starling-7B, and UltraRM-13B despite having 4-5 orders of magnitude fewer parameters. Achieves approximately 1000x speedup in FLOPs per sample (~10^6 vs ~10^9-10^10). Also has a logit-only variant that works with closed-source LLMs (MATH average 52.8). Selective layer experiments show that using only layers {16, 24, 28, 32} maintains most performance.

**Direct comparison to PAMH:** This is the most directly comparable work -- both claim hidden-state reward signals with <0.005% parameters. ELHSR uses a single linear layer with gating over all layers, while PAMH would need to differentiate its architectural contribution.

---

## 3. CoRGI (arXiv 2508.00378) -- Verified Chain-of-Thought with Visual Grounding

**Authors:** Shixin Yi, Lin Shang (Nanjing University, August 2025)

**Step-wise visual grounding verification pipeline (3 stages):**

1. **Reasoning generation:** VLM generates a multi-step reasoning chain R = {r_1, r_2, ..., r_n} from image + question.

2. **Visual Evidence Verification Module (VEVM)** -- for each reasoning step r_i:
   - **Relevance Classifier:** Lightweight MLP determines if the step requires visual verification (binary gate + importance weight 0-100%)
   - **RoI Selector:** Grounding DINO (zero-shot) identifies relevant image regions via bounding boxes based on the textual step content
   - **Evidence Extractor:** A VLM acts as a "fact checker," generating concise grounded descriptions of visual content within the identified RoIs. Falls back to full image if no RoIs selected.

3. **Final synthesis:** VLM processes question + reasoning chain + all visual evidence (with importance weights) to produce the verified final answer.

**Key insight:** This is post-hoc verification -- it does not modify the generation process but verifies each reasoning step against actual visual evidence after generation, filtering or correcting unsupported claims.

**Results (improvements over raw VLM):**
- Qwen-2.5VL-7B: VCR Q->AR +8.4, MMMU +2.1, MathVista +0.9, HallusionBench +0.9
- LLaVA-1.6-7B: VCR QA->R +12.9, ScienceQA +5.7, HallusionBench +3.6
- Gemma3-12B: MathVista +4.9, VCR QA->R +4.3, ScienceQA +2.4

Ablations confirm every sub-module contributes. A 380M end-to-end trained variant failed due to step repetition and hallucinated grounding, motivating the modular VLM-based approach.

---

## 4. Vision-SR1 (arXiv 2508.19652) -- Self-Rewarding VLM

**Authors:** Zhanpeng Li et al. (August 2025)

**Method:** A three-stage self-rewarding RL framework using two rollout passes of the same VLM:

- **First pass** (with image): (Image, Query) -> generates structured output in "See-Think" format:
  - `<visual_reasoning>c</visual_reasoning>` -- self-contained visual perception
  - `<think>t</think>` -- language reasoning
  - `<answer>a</answer>` -- final answer
  - Accuracy reward: r_ans = I[a == a*]

- **Second pass** (without image): (Query, Visual Perception c only) -> generates new reasoning and answer
  - Self-visual reward: r_visual = I[a_hat == a*]
  - If the model can derive the correct answer from the perception text alone (without the image), the perception is deemed faithful.

**RL algorithm:** Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with multi-reward policy optimization. Key innovation: separate Z-score normalization and KL penalties for visual and answer reward streams, preventing entangled learning signals.

**Training data:** Vision-SR1-47K -- 47K examples from 24 benchmarks (30.5% math, 30% science, 39.5% general visual reasoning).

**Results (Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, average across 7 benchmarks): 52.2** vs Vision-R1 50.7. Notable gains:
- HallusionBench: 68.9 (vs 66.6)
- RealWorldQA: 69.2 (vs 66.6)
- MATH-Vision: 36.2 (vs 33.8)
- Also tested on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Mimo-VL-7B with consistent improvements

Reduces Language Shortcut Rate. Spatial reasoning gains: MMSI-Bench 28.0% (vs 21.9%), OmniSpatial 44.2% (vs 31.1%). Computational overhead: only ~20% more than standard GRPO (13 vs 10.5 hours). No external reward models needed.

---

## 5. VRPRM (arXiv 2508.03556) -- Process Reward Modeling via Visual Reasoning

**Authors:** Xinquan Chen, Chongying Yue, Bangwei Liu, Xuhong Wang, Yingchun Wang, Chaochao Lu (August 2025)

**Architecture:** A genuinely multimodal CoT-PRM built on three base models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, MiMo-VL-7B-SFT, and Qwen3-4B-VL-Thinking. Outputs `<think>...</think>` reasoning tokens followed by boxed correctness scores and structured JSON results per step.

**Two-stage training:**
1. **Cold Start SFT (Stage 1):** 3.6K high-quality CoT-PRM examples (from ~10K VisualPRM400K samples, annotated by Claude-3.7-Sonnet with 3-step prompting). LoRA rank 16, alpha 32, LR 1e-4, 3 epochs. Balanced positive/negative ratio.
2. **RL Scaling (Stage 2):** GRPO on 50K non-CoT PRM samples. Reward = 0.1 * format compliance + 0.9 * process accuracy. LR 1e-6, KL penalty 1e-6, batch size 512.

**Results:**

**Authors:** Si Wang et al. (June 2025)

**Proxy task design:** Starting from PixMo-Cap dataset (384K images with detailed ~200-word captions), GPT-4 injects a single subtle visual hallucination -- altering a few words to create errors in one of 8 categories: object, attribute, count, spatial, color, material, shape, or text. **Reward:** Binary exact-match (0.9 weight) + format compliance (0.1 weight). Total training data: 875K image-caption pairs after filtering.

  "core_problem": "Vision-language models (VLMs) performing multi-step visual reasoning suffer from 'evidence collapse' — progressively losing visual grounding during reasoning even as they produce confident text (Don't Blink, arXiv 2604.04207). While lightweight probes on VLM hidden states can detect hallucination risk pre-generation (HALP achieves 0.93 AUROC) and training-time perception RL methods improve perception quality, NO existing approach provides near-zero-cost STEP-LEVEL PROCESS monitoring during generation that DECOMPOSES perception errors from reasoning errors. VerifySteer (arXiv 2605.20745) discovers that verifier strictness is encoded at step boundaries in hidden states, but operates exclusively on text-only LLMs and cannot monitor visual evidence. SIEVE (arXiv 2603.14117) provides visual evidence re-engagement via internal representations, but offers no error monitoring or decomposition — it re-engages vision without knowing WHEN or WHY re-engagement is needed. Can we distill step-level perception-error expertise from multimodal PRMs into a near-zero-cost auxiliary head that monitors evidence collapse in real time, providing DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning error signals that enable TARGETED interventions at each reasoning step?",
  "opportunity": "A precise technical gap exists at the intersection of four established capabilities: (1) VLM hidden states encode reliable visual evidence and correctness signals — probes achieve 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection (HALP), 0.96 AUROC for correctness prediction (Gnosis), and >92% accuracy for reliability flagging (arXiv 2508.18297). (2) Multimodal PRMs encode rich STEP-LEVEL perception-error expertise — URSA-RM-8B's DualMath-1.1M dataset with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, VisualPRM-8B's 400K process supervision samples, EVPV's explicit visual premise verification achieving 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench, VRPRM's CoT-PRM achieving 66.00 AEI with only 53.6K training examples — that captures error PATTERNS across steps, not just binary outcomes. (3) VLMs demonstrably suffer from evidence collapse during multi-step reasoning — 'Don't Blink' shows 53-90% loss of visual attention mass as reasoning unfolds, with the 'confident-but-blind' pattern causing 15-40pp higher error rates. (4) Complementary approaches provide re-engagement mechanisms but not monitoring: SIEVE re-engages visual evidence via internal representations achieving 8% average gain by injecting cached region embeddings; DLR (arXiv 2604.07518) provides step-wise visual re-grounding via 32 learned latent queries achieving MathVista 67.5%; Entropy-Gradient Grounding (arXiv 2604.08456) offers training-free evidence retrieval via entropy-gradient relevance maps. These re-engagement methods need a TRIGGER — they lack the ability to detect WHEN and WHY re-engagement is needed. The gap: existing online monitoring approaches (PSRD) operate on descriptive captioning only, cost 4× inference time, and treat all hallucinations uniformly without decomposition; step-boundary hidden-state signals (VerifySteer) work only for text-only LLMs; evidence re-engagement methods (SIEVE, DLR) lack monitoring capability; and existing probes (HALP, VIB-Probe, EnsemHalDet, SWIFT, LiLaVe) operate on OUTCOME-LEVEL binary labels without step-level process understanding or error-type decomposition. The opportunity: PRM-distilled step-level supervision provides richer training signal than either binary outcome labels (used by HALP/SWIFT/LiLaVe) or self-reward signals (used by PSRD), capturing temporal error patterns (how evidence collapse propagates across steps) and error-type decomposition (perception vs. reasoning) that outcome-supervised probes and self-reward mechanisms inherently cannot learn. This enables a monitoring head that detects evidence collapse AS IT HAPPENS during generation, at probe-level cost but with PRM-level process understanding — and critically, provides DECOMPOSED error signals that can trigger TARGETED interventions (visual evidence re-engagement for perception errors, backtracking for reasoning errors) rather than one-size-fits-all corrections.",
  "landscape": "**VLM Hidden-State Probing for Error Detection (established but limited to outcome-level):** HALP (EACL 2026, arXiv 2603.05465) trains lightweight 3-layer MLP probes on VLM hidden states, achieving 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection pre-generation across 8 modern VLMs — the most direct baseline for any auxiliary-head approach. VIB-Probe (arXiv 2601.05547, Jan 2026) applies variational information bottleneck to VLM attention heads, achieving 95.92% AUROC on POPE with inference-time mitigation capability. EnsemHalDet (arXiv 2604.02784, Apr 2026) trains ensemble of logistic regression classifiers on hidden states + attention, achieving 0.874 AUC at <0.002s per sample. 'Reading Between the Lines' (arXiv 2511.19806) trains 4-layer MLP probes on VLM hidden states specifically for OCR perception errors — finding intermediate layers 15-20 most informative. 'Anatomy of a Lie'/CAD (arXiv 2603.15557, Mar 2026) uses information-theoretic probes mapping VLM generation to a 'Cognitive State Space' and decomposes hallucinations into perceptual instability, inferential conflict, and decisional ambiguity — sharing our decomposition motivation but using unsupervised anomaly detection rather than PRM-distilled supervision. REVERSE (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2504.13169) trains VLMs for on-the-fly self-verification during generation via retrospective resampling, reducing hallucinations by up to 34%. Sample ~50K multimodal math reasoning trajectories from the (optionally perception-RL-trained) Qwen3-VL-8B policy across MathV360K, GeoQA, and MMathCoT problems. Score with VERIFIED-AVAILABLE teacher PRMs: (a) URSA-RM-8B (PRIMARY — released on HuggingFace URSA-MATH/URSA-RM-8B, DualMath-1.1M training data with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, SAM-B+SigLIP-L+Qwen2.5-Math architecture, covers the same 6 mathematical benchmarks as our evaluation suite; provides broad step-level scoring with particular expertise in visual misinterpretation patterns), (b) VisualPRM-8B (SECONDARY — released on HuggingFace OpenGVLab/VisualPRM-8B, trained on VisualPRM400K, provides step-level process supervision with VisualProcessBench-compatible scoring, InternVL architecture provides cross-family diversity from URSA's Qwen-based design), (c) EVPV (COMPLEMENTARY for decomposition — code released at github.com/Qwen-Applications/EVPV-PRM, provides DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning labels via explicit visual premise verification, SOTA 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench; uniquely contributes the perception vs. reasoning decomposition labels essential for PAMH's dual-head training). AVAILABILITY NOTE: Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583) would be an ideal additional teacher given its token-level perception-centric error grounding and Qwen-VL family compatibility, but its code/weights are NOT released as of May 2026 (RUCAIBox/Perceval GitHub does not exist). Our design is FULLY FUNCTIONAL without Perceval: URSA-RM-8B provides systematic misinterpretation patterns from 302K curated examples, VisualPRM-8B provides broad step-level process scores from 400K samples, and EVPV uniquely provides the perception/reasoning decomposition labels. If Perceval is released during the project timeline, we incorporate it as a fourth teacher for token-level grounding refinement. Extract THREE types of step-level signals beyond binary labels: (i) PRM score DROP trajectories — how error propagates across steps (temporal process patterns that outcome labels cannot capture), computed as score deltas between consecutive steps from URSA-RM-8B and VisualPRM-8B, (ii) perception-specific error flags from EVPV's visual premise verification (which steps involve perceptual vs. reasoning errors), cross-validated with URSA-RM-8B's misinterpretation-sensitive scoring (steps where visual misinterpretation causes score drops), (iii) evidence collapse indicators — attention mass decrease between consecutive steps (from 'Don't Blink' methodology applied to training trajectories). Validate via human annotation on 500-sample subset measuring inter-PRM agreement and error-type classification accuracy.\n\nPhase 2 — PAMH Training with Process-Level Supervision. Three-stage curriculum: (2a) Warm-up: freeze VLM backbone, train PAMH on PRM-labeled trajectories with multi-task loss: binary cross-entropy for perception-error and reasoning-error heads PLUS auxiliary regression loss predicting step-level PRM score (providing richer gradient than binary labels alone — this is the key difference from HALP-style direct probing and SWIFT-style outcome-level reward extraction). Layer selection: intermediate layers 16-24 as primary features based on 'Reading Between the Lines' findings, with ablation against deep layers 24-32 ('Seeing but Not Believing') and all-layer concatenation (SWIFT-style). (2b) Joint fine-tuning: unfreeze backbone with gradient scaling (lambda=0.1-0.3) on PAMH loss, KL regularization (beta=0.01) against original policy to preserve perception RL improvements from Phase 0. (2c) Perception-error curriculum: oversample trajectories exhibiting evidence collapse (identified by attention mass decrease >50% between steps 1 and step N) and EVPV-flagged visual misinterpretation, weighted 3x.\n\nPhase 3 — Inference-Time Monitoring with Targeted Intervention Protocol. During generation, PAMH provides step-quality estimates at each step boundary (identified analogously to VerifySteer's paragraph-boundary approach, validated by their finding that hidden states at delimiters encode verification-relevant signals, but operating on multimodal hidden states rather than text-only). Monitoring is decomposed with TARGETED interventions: (a) When P(perception_error) exceeds calibrated threshold tau_p, trigger SIEVE-inspired visual evidence re-engagement — inject cached region embeddings from gradient-salient image patches back into the reasoning chain (leveraging SIEVE's validated mechanism that middle-layer hidden states enable effective cross-modal matching without image re-encoding; alternatively, use Entropy-Gradient Grounding's training-free approach for lighter-weight region localization). This is more compute-efficient than Perceval's truncation-regeneration (which requires full response regeneration) and more targeted than PSRD's contrastive decoding (which adjusts decoding globally without diagnosing the error type). (b) When P(reasoning_error) exceeds tau_r, trigger standard backtracking and re-generation of the current step. Thresholds calibrated on held-out validation set targeting >80% precision (motivated by 'Don't Blink' finding that false alarms in visual tasks waste compute on benign disengagement). COST ANALYSIS: The PAMH forward pass adds <0.1% compute per step (~0.05ms for 3-5M params). The TOTAL inference-time cost increase including triggered interventions depends on PAMH's precision and error rates: at >80% precision with ~15% step-level error rate, approximately 4% of steps trigger intervention, yielding ~8-12% total compute increase vs. single-pass generation. COMPARATIVE COST-EFFECTIVENESS: (i) vs. PSRD: 4× (300%) inference cost increase on captioning only, with no error decomposition and no demonstrated math reasoning capability — PAMH is 25-30× more cost-efficient per monitored step; (ii) vs. majority voting k=3: 200% cost increase with no decomposition information — PAMH provides decomposed error types enabling targeted interventions at 1/17th the additional cost; (iii) vs. Don't Blink vision veto: zero additional cost but provides only binary 'confident-but-blind' detection without step-level granularity, error decomposition, or active intervention capability — PAMH's 8-12% cost buys decomposed, step-level diagnosis enabling differentiated interventions (image re-examination vs. backtracking); (iv) vs. VerifySteer: requires separate verification traces on text-only LLMs — PAMH monitors DURING generation on multimodal models; (v) vs. Perceval iterative: 400-1600% cost for k=4-16 iterations — PAMH achieves comparable monitoring at <1/30th the cost; (vi) vs. SIEVE: SIEVE provides blanket re-engagement policy; PAMH provides error-type-aware triggering that avoids unnecessary re-engagement on reasoning-only errors, improving intervention efficiency.\n\nEvaluation Design — Systematic Comparison Across All Four Axes (probing, online monitoring, external PRM, training-time RL).\n\nBenchmarks: MathVista (overall + GPS subset), MathVerse (testmini, 6 input variants including vision-only), MathVision, GeoQA, WE-MATH, VisualProcessBench.\n\nBaseline organization:\n(A) Training-time perception methods (no inference monitoring): PEARL (CVPR 2026), MoCA (ICML 2026), PAPO (ICLR 2026), VPPO (ICLR 2026), vanilla GRPO.\n(B) Inference-time monitoring via external PRMs: URSA-RM reranking, VisualPRM reranking, EVPV-enhanced PRM, majority voting.\n(C) Lightweight internalized monitoring: (C1) PAMH-only (no perception RL base), (C2) Perception-RL-only (PEARL-style, no PAMH), (C3) PAMH + perception RL (full method), (C4) Frozen probe baseline (ReProbe-style adapted to multimodal), (C5) VeriThinker-style verification fine-tuning adapted to multimodal.\n(C6) **HALP-style direct probing baseline** — same PAMH architecture but trained on binary ground-truth perception-error labels (correct/incorrect) WITHOUT PRM distillation. This is the CRITICAL ablation: it isolates the value of PRM process-level supervision vs. outcome-level labels for the same architecture.\n(C7) **CAD-style unsupervised probing baseline** — information-theoretic anomaly detection on hidden state trajectories without any supervision.\n(C8) Octopus-style self-correction — controllable correction without explicit monitoring head.\n(C9) **PSRD-adapted baseline** — adapt PSRD's phase-wise self-reward decoding framework to multi-step mathematical reasoning (extending beyond its original captioning domain), using the same CLIP-based reward model approach. This tests whether self-reward signals (without PRM distillation) suffice for math reasoning monitoring. NOTE: this is a good-faith extension since PSRD was not evaluated on math reasoning; we report both its original captioning results and our adaptation.\n(C10) **SIEVE-adapted baseline** — SIEVE's RL-learned visual re-engagement policy applied to our math reasoning trajectories without PAMH's decomposed monitoring. This tests whether blanket re-engagement (SIEVE's approach) vs. targeted monitoring-triggered re-engagement (PAMH's approach) is more effective.\n(C11) **SWIFT-style linear baseline** — single linear transformation on all-layer concatenated hidden states (SWIFT architecture) applied to multimodal VLM, trained with PRM step-level labels. Tests whether PAMH's two-stream architecture provides value over extreme-efficiency linear approach.\n\nKey ablations: (i) PRM-distilled supervision (C3) vs. direct outcome-label probing (C6) — the CENTRAL experiment justifying PRM distillation; (ii) PRM-distilled (C3) vs. self-reward monitoring (C9/PSRD-adapted) — tests whether PRM expertise adds value over self-reward signals for math reasoning; (iii) URSA-RM-only vs. VisualPRM-only vs. EVPV-only vs. multi-teacher — validates complementarity of teacher PRMs; (iv) intermediate-layer (16-24) vs. deep-layer (24-32) vs. all-layer hidden states (SWIFT-style); (v) decomposed (perception+reasoning) vs. unified error detection — isolates decomposition value; (vi) with vs. without attention-engagement stream (ablating 'Don't Blink' signals); (vii) Phase 0 with vs. without perception RL base; (viii) PAMH architecture variants (linear/2-layer/Gnosis-style two-stream/SWIFT-style single linear C11); (ix) step-level PRM regression loss vs. binary-only loss; (x) PAMH-triggered targeted re-engagement vs. SIEVE blanket re-engagement (C10) — tests whether decomposed monitoring improves intervention efficiency; (xi) SIEVE-inspired region embedding injection vs. text-based re-examination prompt for perception-error intervention.\n\nPrimary hypotheses: (H1) PAMH achieves at least 90% of external PRM-guided accuracy at <5% of PRM inference FLOPs; (H2) PAMH + perception RL base outperforms either alone by at least 2% on perception-heavy subsets (MathVista-GPS, MathVerse vision-only); (H3) PRM-distilled PAMH (C3) outperforms direct-probe PAMH (C6) by at least 3% on step-level error detection (VisualProcessBench) because PRM distillation provides: (a) richer step-level process labels capturing error propagation patterns, (b) error-type decomposition from EVPV supervision, and (c) systematic perception-error patterns from URSA's 302K misinterpretation corpus that binary outcome labels cannot encode; (H4) The attention-engagement stream significantly improves detection of evidence-collapse errors specifically (validated on 'Don't Blink'-style analysis); (H5) PRM-distilled PAMH outperforms PSRD-adapted baseline (C9) on multi-step math reasoning, demonstrating that systematic PRM expertise is superior to self-reward signals for complex reasoning domains where PSRD's captioning-oriented approach has no demonstrated capability;   "core_problem": "Vision-language models (VLMs) performing multi-step visual reasoning suffer from 'evidence collapse' — progressively losing visual grounding during reasoning even as they produce confident text (Don't Blink, arXiv 2604.04207). While lightweight probes on VLM hidden states can detect hallucination risk pre-generation (HALP achieves 0.93 AUROC) and training-time perception RL methods improve perception quality, NO existing approach provides near-zero-cost STEP-LEVEL PROCESS monitoring during generation that DECOMPOSES perception errors from reasoning errors. Pre-generation probes cannot catch errors that emerge mid-reasoning due to evidence collapse; external PRMs (URSA, VisualPRM, Perceval) provide step-level monitoring but require full model forward passes per verification step; and training-time perception RL (MoCA, PEARL, PAPO, VPPO) improves the base model but offers no inference-time detection mechanism. Recent online monitoring approaches partially address this: PSRD (arXiv 2604.17982) achieves 50% hallucination reduction via phase-wise self-reward decoding, but only on descriptive captioning tasks (not multi-step math reasoning), at 4× inference cost, and without any perception/reasoning error decomposition. VerifySteer (arXiv 2605.20745) discovers that verifier strictness is encoded at step boundaries in hidden states, but operates exclusively on text-only LLMs and cannot monitor visual evidence. SIEVE (arXiv 2603.14117) provides visual evidence re-engagement via internal representations, but offers no error monitoring or decomposition — it re-engages vision without knowing WHEN or WHY re-engagement is needed. Can we distill step-level perception-error expertise from multimodal PRMs into a near-zero-cost auxiliary head that monitors evidence collapse in real time, providing DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning error signals that enable TARGETED interventions at each reasoning step?",
  "opportunity": "A precise technical gap exists at the intersection of four established capabilities: (1) VLM hidden states encode reliable visual evidence and correctness signals — probes achieve 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection (HALP), 0.96 AUROC for correctness prediction (Gnosis), and >92% accuracy for reliability flagging (arXiv 2508.18297). SWIFT (KDD 2026, arXiv 2505.12225) shows that even ~270K parameter (<0.005%) linear transformations on hidden states can serve as effective reward models, and LiLaVe (arXiv 2504.16760) demonstrates lightweight latent verifiers (XGBoost on hidden states) reliably extract correctness from LLM hidden states — both validating extreme efficiency for hidden-state-based verification. (2) Multimodal PRMs encode rich STEP-LEVEL perception-error expertise — URSA-RM-8B's DualMath-1.1M dataset with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, VisualPRM-8B's 400K process supervision samples, EVPV's explicit visual premise verification achieving 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench, VRPRM's CoT-PRM achieving 66.00 AEI with only 53.6K training examples — that captures error PATTERNS across steps, not just binary outcomes. (3) VLMs demonstrably suffer from evidence collapse during multi-step reasoning — 'Don't Blink' shows 53-90% loss of visual attention mass as reasoning unfolds, with the 'confident-but-blind' pattern causing 15-40pp higher error rates. (4) Complementary approaches provide re-engagement mechanisms but not monitoring: SIEVE re-engages visual evidence via internal representations achieving 8% average gain by injecting cached region embeddings; DLR (arXiv 2604.07518) provides step-wise visual re-grounding via 32 learned latent queries achieving MathVista 67.5%; Entropy-Gradient Grounding (arXiv 2604.08456) offers training-free evidence retrieval via entropy-gradient relevance maps. These re-engagement methods need a TRIGGER — they lack the ability to detect WHEN and WHY re-engagement is needed. The gap: existing online monitoring approaches (PSRD) operate on descriptive captioning only, cost 4× inference time, and treat all hallucinations uniformly without decomposition; step-boundary hidden-state signals (VerifySteer) work only for text-only LLMs; evidence re-engagement methods (SIEVE, DLR) lack monitoring capability; and existing probes (HALP, VIB-Probe, EnsemHalDet, SWIFT, LiLaVe) operate on OUTCOME-LEVEL binary labels without step-level process understanding or error-type decomposition. The opportunity: PRM-distilled step-level supervision provides richer training signal than either binary outcome labels (used by HALP/SWIFT/LiLaVe) or self-reward signals (used by PSRD), capturing temporal error patterns (how evidence collapse propagates across steps) and error-type decomposition (perception vs. reasoning) that outcome-supervised probes and self-reward mechanisms inherently cannot learn. This enables a monitoring head that detects evidence collapse AS IT HAPPENS during generation, at probe-level cost but with PRM-level process understanding — and critically, provides DECOMPOSED error signals that can trigger TARGETED interventions (visual evidence re-engagement for perception errors, backtracking for reasoning errors) rather than one-size-fits-all corrections.",
  "landscape": "**VLM Hidden-State Probing for Error Detection (established but limited to outcome-level):** HALP (EACL 2026, arXiv 2603.05465) trains lightweight 3-layer MLP probes on VLM hidden states, achieving 0.93 AUROC for hallucination detection pre-generation across 8 modern VLMs — the most direct baseline for any auxiliary-head approach. Key finding: late query-token states integrating vision+language are most predictive. VIB-Probe (arXiv 2601.05547, Jan 2026) applies variational information bottleneck to VLM attention heads, achieving 95.92% AUROC on POPE with inference-time mitigation capability. EnsemHalDet (arXiv 2604.02784, Apr 2026) trains ensemble of logistic regression classifiers on hidden states + attention, achieving 0.874 AUC at <0.002s per sample. 'Reading Between the Lines' (arXiv 2511.19806) trains 4-layer MLP probes on VLM hidden states specifically for OCR perception errors — finding intermediate layers 15-20 most informative. 'Anatomy of a Lie'/CAD (arXiv 2603.15557, Mar 2026) uses information-theoretic probes mapping VLM generation to a 'Cognitive State Space' and decomposes hallucinations into perceptual instability, inferential conflict, and decisional ambiguity — sharing our decomposition motivation but using unsupervised anomaly detection rather than PRM-distilled supervision. LiLaVe (arXiv 2504.16760, Apr 2025) introduces lightweight latent verifiers that extract correctness signals from LLM hidden states using XGBoost on features from 5 layers × 16 token positions, achieving AUC 0.86-0.93 on math benchmarks (approaching multi-billion-parameter ORM verifiers) with training in ~3 minutes on CPU — validating the probe paradigm for verification but operating at outcome level on text-only LLMs. SWIFT (KDD 2026, arXiv 2505.12225) mines intrinsic rewards from LLM hidden states via single linear transformation with ~270K parameters (<0.005% of EurusRM-7B), using gated token-level reward aggregation: for each token, concatenates all-layer hidden states and applies W_SWIFT to produce (gate, reward) pairs, achieving 12.7% higher accuracy than EurusRM-7B on MATH — the most parameter-efficient hidden-state reward approach, but text-only and outcome-level with no step-level process monitoring or error decomposition. KEY LIMITATION: All these probes train on binary outcome labels (correct/hallucinated) and operate pre-generation or per-response. None provides step-level process monitoring during multi-step reasoning, none can detect evidence collapse as it unfolds across steps, and none decomposes perception from reasoning errors. **Internalized Verification (near-zero-cost but step-agnostic):** Gnosis (arXiv 2512.20578, Dec 2025) trains ~5M parameter self-awareness heads (two-stream: hidden state + attention encoders with gated MLP fusion) achieving 0.96 AUROC, outperforming external judges including Gemini 2.5 Pro — demonstrating that tiny modules can rival massive verifiers. LaSeR (arXiv 2510.14943, Oct 2025) uses last-token self-rewarding via closed-form RL objective, achieving ~80% verification F1 at one-token cost. ReProbe (arXiv 2511.06209) trains <10M param probes matching 7B PRMs. STEP (arXiv 2601.09093) uses hidden states as early signals for trace evaluation. REVERSE (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2504.13169) trains VLMs for on-the-fly self-verification during generation via retrospective resampling, reducing hallucinations by up to 34%. VeriThinker (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2505.17941) trains LLMs to verify then generate. ADPO (arXiv 2601.01483) jointly trains generation + outcome-level verification. KEY LIMITATION: All internalized verifiers either (a) operate at outcome level only (Gnosis, LaSeR, ADPO, LiLaVe, SWIFT), (b) use binary labels without error-type decomposition (all), or (c) operate on text-only hidden states missing visual features (ReProbe, STEP, LaSeR, SWIFT, LiLaVe). None combines PRM-distilled step-level supervision with multimodal hidden states for decomposed perception/reasoning monitoring. **Online Monitoring During Generation (emerging but limited):** PSRD (arXiv 2604.17982, Apr 2026) achieves online hallucination monitoring during VLM generation via phase-wise self-reward decoding — discovering that hallucination severity peaks at the onset of each semantic phase and using a CLIP-based reward model for guided contrastive decoding intervention. Achieves 50% CHAIR reduction on LLaVA-1.5-7B (CHAIR 7.8→3.9) and reduces hallucination accumulation rate from 0.35%/phase to 0.07%/phase, tested across InstructBLIP-7B, LLaVA-NeXT-7B, LLaVA-1.5-13B. KEY LIMITATIONS: (a) tested exclusively on descriptive captioning/visual understanding (AMBER, POPE, Object HalBench) — no multi-step mathematical reasoning evaluation whatsoever; (b) treats all hallucinations uniformly without perception/reasoning decomposition; (c) 4× inference cost is substantially higher than probe-level monitoring; (d) uses self-elicited confidence signals which capture surface-level patterns rather than systematic error expertise from curated datasets; (e) phase segmentation relies on simple punctuation delimiters rather than learned step boundaries. VerifySteer (arXiv 2605.20745, May 2026) discovers that verifier strictness is encoded in hidden states at paragraph-boundary delimiter tokens (specifically layer 22, double-newline tokens), enabling selective latent steering via offline-constructed steering vectors (d_strict, d_lenient) with sample-level routing through a lightweight 3-layer MLP correctness probe. Matches self-consistency at 4-7× less compute on ProcessBench and Hard2Verify; surpasses Qwen3-14B with only Qwen3-8B + steering. KEY LIMITATIONS: (a) exclusively text-only LLM verification — no visual modality, cannot monitor visual evidence collapse; (b) addresses verifier calibration (over-critical vs under-critical mistakes), not evidence collapse detection or error-type decomposition; (c) requires paragraph-boundary structure with \\n\\n delimiters that may not generalize across generation formats. PSRD and VerifySteer together validate two key premises of our approach — that online monitoring during generation is valuable (PSRD) and that hidden states at step boundaries encode useful signals (VerifySteer) — but neither provides MULTIMODAL, DECOMPOSED, NEAR-ZERO-COST step-level monitoring for multi-step reasoning. **Evidence Collapse and Visual Grounding Loss / Re-engagement:** 'Don't Blink' (arXiv 2604.04207, Apr 2026) demonstrates that VLMs lose 53-90% of attention to visual evidence during multi-step reasoning — the 'evidence collapse' phenomenon. Proposes a 'vision veto' policy detecting 'confident-but-blind' predictions via entropy-vision interaction models at zero additional cost, achieving 1.9pp selective risk reduction. 'Seeing but Not Believing' (arXiv 2510.17771, Oct 2025) shows VLMs encode reliable visual evidence in deep layers but under-utilize it. SPARC (arXiv 2602.06566) separates perception/reasoning circuits for test-time scaling. SIEVE (arXiv 2603.14117, Mar 2026) is an end-to-end self-revisit framework that re-engages visual evidence during reasoning via internal representations — using gradient saliency to identify textual anchors, matching to image patches via cosine similarity in middle-layer hidden states, and injecting cached region embeddings back into the reasoning chain without image re-encoding. Trained via RL (GRPO) on ~1,500 COCO samples, achieves 8% average improvement including WeMath +20.65%. KEY INSIGHT: SIEVE provides a concrete RE-ENGAGEMENT mechanism but not a monitoring mechanism — it learns when to re-engage via RL policy without explicitly diagnosing error types. DLR (arXiv 2604.07518, Apr 2026) decomposes reasoning into premise-look-reason cycles with learned latent visual grounder using 32 learnable queries on a Spherical Gaussian Latent Policy, achieving MathVista 67.5% (+5.0%). 3-stage training pipeline (pretraining, SFT, RL). Entropy-Gradient Grounding (arXiv 2604.08456, Apr 2026) provides training-free evidence retrieval via entropy-gradient relevance maps — using next-token distribution entropy backpropagated to visual embeddings for multi-region localization with spatial-entropy stopping rule, achieving +14.82 on TextVQA and +15.71 on V*Bench across 4 VLM architectures. KEY INSIGHT: evidence collapse is a TEMPORAL phenomenon — models may start well-grounded and become blind by step 3 — making pre-generation probes insufficient and step-level monitoring essential. Re-engagement methods (SIEVE, DLR, Entropy-Gradient Grounding) address the RESPONSE but not the DETECTION; PAMH provides the detection and decomposition signal that can trigger these interventions. **Training-Time Perception-Aware RL (training-only, no inference monitoring):** MoCA (ICML 2026 Spotlight, arXiv 2605.14054) — modality-aware credit assignment, 73.8 MathVista. PEARL (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2511.18437) — perception checklists, +9.7% MathVerse. PDCR (arXiv 2605.13467) — decomposed confidence rewards. PRCO (arXiv 2603.28618) — Observer/Solver coevolution. PAPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2507.06448) — implicit perception loss, 30.5% perception error reduction. VPPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.09285) — visual dependency advantages. PeBR (arXiv 2509.13031) — two-stage perception-first RL. Perception-R1 (arXiv 2506.07218) — visual perception reward. 'From Seeing to Thinking' (arXiv 2605.20177) — staged perception-then-reasoning. G1 (arXiv 2505.13426) — perception-reasoning mutual bootstrapping. PROPA (arXiv 2511.10279) — MCTS+GRPO process-level optimization. Vision-SR1 (arXiv 2508.19652, Aug 2025) — self-rewarding VLM via reasoning decomposition into visual and language components with decoupled reward-advantage framework; two-pass approach (with/without image) where self-visual reward validates perception faithfulness. Shares our perception/reasoning decomposition motivation but operates at training time, not inference monitoring, and requires a second forward pass for self-reward extraction. ViCrit (arXiv 2506.10128, Jun 2025) — verifiable RL proxy task training VLMs to localize synthetic visual hallucinations injected into captions; demonstrates strong transfer to MathVista (+2.5%), MathVerse (+6.5%) from perception proxy task, validating that perception-focused training improves reasoning. None provides inference-time step monitoring. **External Multimodal PRMs (rich supervision sources, expensive at inference):** URSA-RM-8B (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2501.04686) — DualMath-1.1M training data with 302K curated misinterpretation-insertion examples, SAM-B+SigLIP-L+Qwen2.5-Math architecture. Model weights RELEASED on HuggingFace (URSA-MATH/URSA-RM-8B). Evaluated on MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, GeoQA, WE-MATH — matching our benchmark suite. VisualPRM-8B (arXiv 2503.10291) — 8B VLM PRM trained on VisualPRM400K with VisualProcessBench (2,866 samples, 26,950 human-annotated step labels). Model weights and benchmark fully RELEASED (OpenGVLab/VisualPRM-8B, OpenGVLab/VisualProcessBench). Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, Apr 2026) provides perception-centric PRM with token-level error grounding and truncation-regeneration. CRITICAL NOTE: code and model weights NOT released as of May 2026 despite the paper's stated intent; the RUCAIBox/Perceval GitHub repository does not exist. EVPV/'Grounding the Score' (arXiv 2603.16253) — decouples perceptual from reasoning errors via explicit visual premise verification, SOTA 67.46% F1 on VisualProcessBench. Code RELEASED (github.com/Qwen-Applications/EVPV-PRM). VL-PRM (arXiv 2509.23250) — shows smaller VL-PRMs match larger ones. MM-PRM (arXiv 2505.13427) — 700K+ MCTS-based step annotations. Athena-PRM (arXiv 2506.09532) — SOTA with only 5K samples. VRPRM (arXiv 2508.03556, Aug 2025) — first multimodal Chain-of-Thought PRM trained via RL (3.6K CoT-PRM SFT examples + 50K GRPO samples), achieving AEI 66.00 on VisualProcessBench, outperforming VisualPRM with only 13.4% of its training data. Demonstrates data-efficient PRM training but operates at full model cost. CoRGI (arXiv 2508.00378, Aug 2025, withdrawn) — proposed step-wise claim decomposition with post-hoc visual grounding via Grounding DINO + VLM fact-checking, tested on VCR, ScienceQA, MMMU, MathVista. Withdrawn by authors citing immaturity. **VLM Self-Correction:** Octopus-8B (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.08503) achieves SOTA VLM self-correction (82.1% MathVista) via correction-specific rollout augmentation. 'Aha Moment Revisited' (arXiv 2506.17417) shows VLM self-verification consistently underperforms majority voting. Sherlock (arXiv 2505.22651) finds self-correction activates in <10% of samples. **Our unique position:** We are the first to distill STEP-LEVEL PROCESS reward signals (not binary outcomes, not self-reward) from multimodal PRMs into a near-zero-cost auxiliary head that monitors evidence collapse during generation with DECOMPOSED perception/reasoning error signals enabling TARGETED interventions.
